I registered an interaction test asking whether PTEN loss concentrates STAT3 dependency more strongly in PIK3CA-mutant cells, which would suggest a coherent PI3K/PTEN-STAT3 axis, and a direct estimate in high IFN-gamma cells to test whether inflammatory signaling amplifies the PTEN-loss effect. Second, I added specificity and context checks for the three largest accepted associations: SMARCA4 loss effect among ARID1A-intact cells tests whether the SMARCA2 vulnerability depends on ARID1A co-loss; MSI-high WRN effect among higher mutation burden distinguishes MSI-high specificity from a general hypermutation proxy; KEAP1 loss effect among STK11-loss cells tests whether the reversed NFE2L2 association persists in a co-mutation context. Third, I broadened pathway hypotheses: BRAF V600E may weaken upstream RIT1 dependency because downstream MAPK activation reduces upstream node dependency; KRAS mutation may weaken EGFR dependency for the same reason. MYC amplification was null overall for POLR2A and RPL11, so I test high-MYC-expression contexts where MYC-driven transcriptional/translational demand should be most relevant. TP53 loss is tested against USP7 dependency because of their shared p53-pathway biology. Finally, I test the STK11-loss effect on KRAS dependency within KRAS-mutant cells as a reverse perspective to H48, which tested the KRAS-mutation effect within STK11-loss cells. All proposals are associations within this dataset, not causal claims.","analyze":"I selected 12 untested analyses that combine robustness for the newly accepted PTEN/STAT3 association, resolution of the borderline KRAS/STK11 pattern, specificity checks for the large accepted associations, and a few broad mechanistic tests. H57 and H58 stratify PTEN-loss STAT3-dependency effect by CRISPR library. If the large H17 effect remains positive in both Avana and non-Avana screens, it is less likely to be a library artifact; attenuation in non-Avana would make the accepted association library-conditional within this dataset. H62 and H63 directly test the logic behind H48: H62 asks whether the KRAS-mutation effect on KRAS dependency is stronger in STK11-loss cells than in STK11-intact cells, while H63 estimates the complement effect in STK11-intact cells. Together with H48 and its validation, these can distinguish a context-specific co-mutation effect from a broader KRAS-mutation association diluted by subgroup size. H74 asks the reverse within KRAS-mutant cells: does STK11 loss itself associate with stronger KRAS dependency? H64 tests whether PTEN-loss effects on STAT3 are stronger in PIK3CA-mutant cells, probing a coherent PI3K/PTEN context. H66, H67, and H68 provide complementary specificity/context checks for the very large SMARCA2, WRN, and NFE2L2 associations: SMARCA4-loss effect among ARID1A-intact cells, MSI-high effect among higher mutation-burden cells, and KEAP1-loss effect among STK11-loss cells. These help determine whether the large associations are robust within co-alteration contexts and not solely driven by overlap with nearby alterations. H69 and H70 are cross-pathway tests: BRAF V600E or KRAS mutation may reduce dependency on upstream nodes RIT1 or EGFR if downstream MAPK activation bypasses those upstream inputs. H73 tests USP7 dependency under TP53 loss, a p53-pathway-related hypothesis not previously examined for this outcome. I did not select high-MYC-expression POLR2A/RPL11 refinements this batch because MYC amplification was null overall and the pathway context is less mature than the selected robustness/co-mutation and MAPK checks.","appraise":"These results mostly strengthen or contextualize the large accepted associations and add one new large mechanistic association, while leaving the KRAS/STK11 cluster uncertain. H57/R27 tests PTEN loss on STAT3 dependency within Avana screens: signed estimate +0.288 (95% CI +0.232 to +0.343), far above the approximate 0.025 absolute-scale threshold and excluding null in the hypothesis direction. I accept H57 and close it as a robustness stratum supporting H17. H58/R28 is the non-Avana complement: signed estimate +0.092 (95% CI -0.062 to +0.246), but only 27 exposed cells; it is promising in point estimate yet too imprecise to accept or reject. Thus the accepted PTEN/STAT3 association is robust in the major Avana stratum but library-conditional precision remains limited outside Avana.\n\nThe KRAS/STK11 follow-ups remain inconclusive. H62/R29 interaction estimate +0.022 (95% CI -0.024 to +0.067) is near the approximate clinical threshold in the expected direction but crosses null and includes both subthreshold and larger effects. H63/R30 complement KRAS-mutation effect in STK11-intact cells is small, +0.010 (95% CI -0.010 to +0.029), with only its upper end marginally approaching the threshold. H74/R38 reverse test, STK11 loss within KRAS-mutant cells, is +0.014 (95% CI -0.026 to +0.053). The pattern mildly favors a co-mutation-specific effect, but no individual comparison is decisive enough to accept a scientifically meaningful difference. I keep H62 and H74 active and defer H63.\n\nH64/R31 is too imprecise for PIK3CA-mutant context because only 38 cells contribute to one exposed subgroup: interaction estimate +0.001 (95% CI -0.150 to +0.152). I leave it unresolved and deferred rather than reject or interpret the null point estimate.\n\nThe specificity/context checks for the three largest accepted effects are decisive. H66/R32 shows that SMARCA4 loss predicts much stronger SMARCA2 dependency even among ARID1A-intact cells: +0.777 (95% CI +0.756 to +0.798). H67/R33 shows MSI-high predicts much stronger WRN dependency even among higher mutation-burden cells: +0.780 (95% CI +0.749 to +0.811). H68/R34 shows KEAP1 loss predicts weaker NFE2L2 dependency in the hypothesized direction even among STK11-loss cells: +0.775 (95% CI +0.727 to +0.823). These are far beyond the threshold, exclude null, and support that the global H5, H7, and H20 associations are not driven solely by the excluded co-alteration contexts. I accept and close each as informative robustness/context checks.\n\nFor the broad MAPK cross-pathway tests, H69/R35 tests BRAF V600E against weaker RIT1 dependency: signed estimate +0.004 (95% CI -0.025 to +0.033). The point estimate is negligible and the interval barely touches clinically meaningful positive values, so I leave it unresolved and defer. H70/R36 tests KRAS mutation against weaker EGFR dependency: signed estimate -0.010 (95% CI -0.027 to +0.008), opposite direction and below threshold; I reject it. H73/R37 is the strongest new discovery: TP53 loss in the hypothesized +1 direction gives +0.396 (95% CI +0.325 to +0.467). Because positive signed values correspond to higher, less negative USP7 dependency scores, this supports TP53-loss cells having weaker USP7 dependency relative to TP53-intact cells in this dataset. It is large, precise, and scientifically coherent with p53-pathway biology, but I treat it only as a dataset association. I accept H73, keep it active, and request independent validation because it is a new large association and validation would test whether it is reproducible outside this discovery partition rather than whether its discovery estimate is internally strong.","synthesize":"The newly delivered validations substantially strengthen two accepted dataset associations but do not resolve the EGFR-amplification claim. For H5, SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency in the discovery estimate and is independently validated with a signed estimate of +0.786 and an independent interval approximately +0.757 to +0.815. This is far beyond the approximate clinical threshold proxy used for these negative-scale dependency outcomes and excludes null in the hypothesized direction. For SMARCA2, high mutation burden tests whether the very large SMARCA4-loss vulnerability is confounded by hypermutant states. For KRAS dependency, I refine the suggestive KRAS/STK11 cluster by estimating the KRAS-mutation effect among STK11-loss cells that remain TP53-intact, helping distinguish a co-mutation-specific effect from dilution across unrelated TP53-loss states. For WRN, low mutation burden complements the accepted high-burden check and tests whether MSI-high specificity survives in lower-burden backgrounds. Finally, BRCA2-loss is tested against WRN dependency as a new replication-stress/DNA-repair hypothesis. evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: The new batch strongly strengthens the existing large associations and gives informative co-alteration context checks, while leaving the EGFR and some KRAS subgroup questions borderline. H87 and H88 show that TP53 loss remains associated with weaker USP7 dependency in MYC-amplified cells (signed +0.510, 95% CI +0.345 to +0.674) and in CDKN2A-loss cells (signed +0.393, 95% CI +0.239 to +0.548); both are large, exclude null, and are accepted/closed as context strata for H73. H91 and H92 show PTEN loss remains associated with stronger STAT3 dependency under high hypoxia (signed +0.237, CI +0.134 to +0.340) and in STK11-loss cells (signed +0.258, CI +0.134 to +0.382); accepted/closed as robustness contexts for H17. H93 and H94 show KEAP1 loss remains associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency under TP53 loss (+0.810, CI +0.763 to +0.857) and MYC amplification (+0.790, CI +0.729 to +0.850); accepted/closed as robustness contexts for H20. H95 shows SMARCA4-loss association with stronger SMARCA2 dependency is robust among higher mutation-burden cells (+0.795, CI +0.768 to +0.821), supporting that it is not merely a hypermutation proxy; accepted/closed for H5. H96 is the key borderline positive: KRAS mutation is associated with stronger KRAS dependency among STK11-loss, TP53-intact cells (signed +0.052, CI +0.008 to +0.096; exposed n=88). The point exceeds the approximate threshold and the interval excludes null, and this refines the suggestive KRAS/STK11 cluster, so I accept it as a dataset association but keep it active and request independent validation because the lower interval bound is still below the approximate meaningful difference and the finding is subgroup-specific. EGFR amplification remains unresolved: in KRAS-wildtype cells H89 is weak (+0.016, CI -0.014 to +0.046), while in KRAS-mutant cells H90 is intriguing (+0.053, CI +0.004 to +0.103) but based on only 43 exposed cells and the overall H2 association is not accepted, so H90 remains unresolved active rather than accepted. H97 cannot be estimated because there are no MSI-high observations in the low-mutation-burden eligibility; this closes that impossible stratum without interpreting it as null. H98 gives a near-zero BRCA2-loss/WRN estimate (-0.00008, CI -0.045 to +0.045), so the directional hypothesis is unsupported but the interval is too wide to confidently exclude a small meaningful effect; deferred. All accepted statements remain dataset associations, not causal or generally validated biological mechanisms.

Study instructions:

results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: The newly delivered validations materially weaken the KRAS/STK11 subgroup cluster and do not support the refined KRAS-mutation effect among STK11-loss TP53-intact cells. For H48, the direct STK11-loss stratification is now assessed with both discovery and independent validation. Discovery gave signed +0.031 with a 95% interval crossing null, and independent validation gave signed +0.043 with an independent interval approximately -0.024 to +0.109. The point estimates favor stronger KRAS dependency in KRAS-mutant STK11-loss cells, and some of the interval range includes clinically meaningful differences under the approximate relative threshold, but the independent interval also includes null, opposite-direction effects, and clearly subthreshold values. Therefore H48 remains unresolved rather than accepted. Because the less-refined H48 estimate is not decisive and the refined H96 estimate failed validation, I defer H48 rather than keep it as a primary active claim, while leaving related KRAS co-mutation interactions in the investigation pool. H96 is explicitly reassessed and downgraded from provisional acceptance to unresolved and closed. Its discovery estimate was signed +0.052 with a borderline interval excluding null, but independent validation returned signed +0.017 with a wide interval approximately -0.058 to +0.092. The validation point estimate is below the approximate 10% relative significance proxy on the usual scale of these dependency outcomes and cannot confirm the subgroup-specific association. The most defensible conclusion is that the KRAS-mutation stronger-dependency signal in STK11-loss TP53-intact cells is not reproduced at a clinically meaningful or statistically decisive level in the supplied data. This does not alter the larger validated associations: H5 SMARCA4 loss associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency and H73 TP53 loss associated with weaker USP7 dependency remain accepted and validated. The other accepted associations H7 MSI-high associated with much stronger WRN dependency, H17 PTEN loss associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, and H20 KEAP1 loss associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency also remain accepted, though not all have independent validation. The failed KRAS refinement is a useful caution against overinterpreting borderline subgroup findings. Next investigation should focus on technical QC and histologic robustness of the validated large associations, EGFR conditional effects, and whether the KRAS co-mutation cluster is better explained by TP53-loss rather than TP53-intact STK11-loss subgroups.

record.narrative: I will prioritize three complementary kinds of comparisons. First, I register high-value robustness strata for the core accepted dataset associations. H5 and H73 are already independently validated, but H7 MSI-high/WRN, H17 PTEN-loss/STAT3, and H20 KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 are not; therefore additional strong and precise stratum estimates could motivate later validation. Serum context, proliferation rate, EMT phenotype, and lineage provide non-CRISPR technical/biological settings in which to ask whether the large accepted effects are stable or context-dependent. These are still dataset associations, not external validation. Second, I focus on unresolved receptor-tyrosine-kinase amplification questions. ERBB2 amplification is null overall in H3, but it may be histology-dependent; an interaction with adenocarcinoma versus squamous can test whether the direct H51/H52 subgroup analyses are masking a context-specific effect. For EGFR amplification, H89 is weak overall in KRAS-wildtype cells and H90 is underpowered but suggestive in KRAS-mutant cells; the proposed KRAS-wildtype/adenocarcinoma stratum is a biologically coherent condition in which EGFR amplification might confer stronger EGFR dependency without KRAS bypass. Third, I introduce new but plausible biological probes: MYC amplification and mitotic KIF18A dependency, TP53 loss and DHX9 replication-stress dependency, KRAS mutation and weaker BRAF dependency from pathway bypass, TP53 loss and MDM2 dependency among high MYC-expression cells where the p53-MDM2 axis may be most relevant, and BRCA2-loss/WRN dependency among MSI-negative cells to ask whether BRCA2 has an effect independent of the dominant MSI-high WRN signal. For these dependency outcomes, a 10% relative difference corresponds to roughly a mean score difference in the low hundredths to few tenths depending on the outcome mean; very large accepted effects are far above this, while smaller receptor-tyrosine-kinase or co-mutation effects will require tight confidence intervals before being accepted.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: This batch delivers decisive robustness evidence for the accepted core dataset associations and several informative negative or inconclusive new probes. For H59, PTEN loss remains associated with much stronger STAT3 dependency under adequate Cas9 activity (signed estimate +0.224, 95% CI +0.159 to +0.289; exposed n=161). The effect is large, excludes null, and is far above the approximate 10% relative threshold for STAT3 dependency (roughly a 0.028 mean-score shift near the overall STAT3 mean), so it is accepted and closed as a QC robustness stratum for H17. H105 strengthens H17 further: in high-EMT cells, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency (+0.378, CI +0.261 to +0.495; exposed n=58). Although the exposed cell is modest, the interval is tight enough and the effect is well above the approximate threshold; accepted and closed. H106 and H107 similarly confirm the KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 and MSI-high/WRN associations in a high-serum culture context: KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency is enormous (+0.814, CI +0.788 to +0.840), and MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency remains enormous (+0.784, CI +0.746 to +0.823). Both exclude null, are far above clinically meaningful thresholds for those outcomes, and are accepted as robustness strata and closed. H77 confirms that TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency even under adequate Cas9 activity (+0.426, CI +0.339 to +0.513), far above the approximate 0.018 threshold for USP7 dependency; accepted and closed. Because H17 now has strong overall and robustness evidence but lacks independent validation, I request independent validation of H17 rather than H7 or H20, whose effects are already extraordinarily precise. The new KRAS co-mutation interaction H86 is not supportive of the claimed TP53-loss-specific enhancement of KRAS dependency (signed interaction -0.018, CI -0.060 to +0.025). Given the failed and imprecise prior KRAS/STK11 refinements and the interval remaining compatible with only a small positive interaction, this is inconclusive but not worth further follow-up; I mark it unresolved and closed. H109 rejects the claimed adenocarcinoma-specific ERBB2 amplification effect: the interaction is negative (-0.051, CI -0.117 to +0.015), and the upper bound is below the approximate 0.026 clinically meaningful threshold for ERBB2 dependency, so a scientifically meaningful adenocarcinoma-enhanced ERBB2 dependency is not supported. H112 rejects TP53 loss associated with stronger DHX9 dependency: the signed estimate is negative (-0.020, CI -0.039 to -0.001), indicating the opposite direction, though not a strongly meaningful reversed effect worth promoting now. H113 rejects KRAS mutation associated with weaker BRAF dependency (+0? signed -0.016, CI -0.034 to +0.001; claimed positive/upper below threshold). H111, H114, and H115 remain unresolved and deferred: each point estimate is below or near the approximate clinical threshold and the intervals are too broad or include null; further follow-up is possible but should not crowd out more robust core claims. All statements remain observational associations within this supplied dataset, not causal mechanisms or claims of external generalizability.

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

record.narrative:
The newly delivered validation materially strengthens the current core evidence base. First, H17 is now independently validated: PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency with signed discovery estimate +0.267, 95% CI +0.215 to +0.319, and independent validation estimate +0.307, independent CI +0.228 to +0.387. Both exclude null and far exceed the approximate 10% relative threshold for STAT3 dependency (roughly +0.028 near the overall mean), so I accept H17 and close its direct investigation while retaining accepted context strata for robustness. Response-deadline claims H5 and H73 are also confirmed. H5 SMARCA4 loss remains associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency in independent validation (+0.786, independent CI +0.757 to +0.815), consistent with discovery (+0.784, CI +0.765 to +0.803). H73 TP53 loss remains associated with weaker USP7 dependency (+0.382, independent CI +0.280 to +0.485), consistent with discovery (+0.396, CI +0.325 to +0.467). These are accepted, validated dataset associations; their investigation is closed because they are now sufficiently characterized and robust across several technical and co-alteration strata.

The current supported findings within this supplied dataset are: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency; PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency; KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency; TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency. All are observational associations among 2000 lung-cell-line profiles with measured predictors, not causal claims or generalizable biological mechanisms. More negative dependency scores mean stronger dependency; positive signed estimates indicate the claimed direction, including the NFE2L2 reversal where KEAP1 loss moves the score toward weaker dependency. H7 and H20 remain accepted without independent validation, but their discovery effects are extremely large and robust across CRISPR library, Cas9 QC, mutation burden, serum, and co-alteration contexts.

Negative or unsupported findings are also informative. BRAF V600E was not associated with stronger BRAF dependency; ERBB2 amplification was not associated with stronger ERBB2 dependency overall and did not show an adenocarcinoma-specific enhancement; MYC amplification was not associated with stronger POLR2A or USP7 dependency; KRAS mutation was not associated with weaker BRAF dependency, stronger RIT1 dependency, or weaker EGFR dependency; TP53 loss was not associated with stronger DHX9 dependency in the claimed direction. Overall EGFR amplification remains a negative/uncertain finding after independent validation: discovery was marginal (R2 +0.025, CI -0.000 to +0.051), validation did not reproduce a clinically meaningful effect (R13 +0.015, independent CI -0.025 to +0.056), so I close H2 as unresolved rather than accepted. Overall KRAS mutation associated with stronger KRAS dependency is also left unresolved and closed as not decisive: the point estimate is below the approximate 10% relative threshold and the interval includes subthreshold values (R4 +0.014, CI -0.004 to +0.031). The KRAS co-mutation subgroup cluster remains weakly supported at best and failed validation in prior refinements, so I am not promoting it further.

Unresolved uncertainty remains around EGFR amplification conditional on KRAS/lineage context, formal lineage heterogeneity for core accepted associations, research-marker associations with TMED10, MYC-related dependencies such as RPL11 and KIF18A, TP53-MDM2 contexts, and BRCA2-related DNA-repair dependencies. The most informative next analyses are independent validation of the two accepted but still non-validated core associations, prioritizing H20 KEAP1 loss and weaker NFE2L2 dependency first, then H7 MSI-high and stronger WRN dependency. In parallel, I registered lineage-interaction proposals for validated core effects and proliferation strata for H20 and H7 to assess heterogeneity and possible confounding by growth rate. These next steps should preserve the distinction between dataset-supported associations and external biological claims.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: This analysis batch is centered on the core dataset-supported dependencies and their stability across biological and screen-quality contexts, while adding one broad MAPK-pathway probe. For the two central accepted but not independently validated associations, I prioritize proliferation and screen-quality strata: H119 and H124 test KEAP1 loss against NFE2L2 dependency in high-growth and high-screen-ROC contexts, respectively; H120 and H125 test MSI-high against WRN dependency in the same contexts. These strata directly assess whether the enormous accepted effects remain clinically meaningful under more stringent biological or technical subsets. For validated core effects, H116-H118 formally test whether the associations vary by lineage subtype: SMARCA4 loss with SMARCA2 dependency, TP53 loss with USP7 dependency, and PTEN loss with STAT3 dependency. These are not intended to change the accepted effects unless the interaction is large and decisive, but they are informative for biological or technical heterogeneity. I also test plausible co-alteration contexts that could affect interpretation of accepted effects: H121 tests PTEN loss within TP53-loss cells for STAT3, H122 tests TP53 loss within KEAP1-loss cells for USP7, and H123 tests KEAP1 loss within ARID1A-loss cells for NFE2L2. H126 tests SMARCA4 loss within high-ploidy cells, a copy-number/aneuploidy context relevant to SMARCA2 dependency. Finally, H130 probes NF1 loss with RIT1 dependency as a broad MAPK-pathway comparison. I am not prioritizing further KRAS co-mutation or EGFR conditional claims now, because prior KRAS refinements failed or remained imprecise and EGFR overall is unresolved after validation. Results should be judged relative to approximate 10% relative thresholds: for most dependency scores near -0.25 this is roughly 0.025-0.03 mean-score shift, while the accepted SMARCA2, WRN, NFE2L2, USP7, and STAT3 effects are far larger. Stable large positive signed estimates in core strata will support later independent validation of H20 and H7; modest, null, or highly imprecise results will be treated as context-specific or inconclusive observational evidence only.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction

Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: This batch strongly reinforces the core dataset associations and gives little support to the new MAPK-pathway or formal lineage-heterogeneity claims. The estimates are already signed to the hypothesis direction, so positive values support the claimed association. H119 shows that KEAP1 loss remains associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency among high-growth-rate cells: signed estimate +0.835, 95% CI +0.793 to +0.879, exposed n=78. This is enormous relative to the approximate 10% relative threshold for dependency_NFE2L2 and excludes the null, so I accept and close this stratum. H120 similarly shows that MSI-high remains associated with much stronger WRN dependency among high-growth-rate cells: +0.785, CI +0.722 to +0.847, exposed n=35. Despite the smaller exposed cell, the estimate is extremely far above the approximate threshold for WRN dependency and excludes null; accepted and closed. H124 and H125 provide screen-quality robustness: MSI-high/WRN +0.790, CI +0.751 to +0.829; KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2 +0.793, CI +0.764 to +0.822. Both are accepted and closed. The co-alteration strata also support the accepted core effects rather than overturning them: H121 PTEN loss within TP53-loss cells for STAT3 is +0.190, CI +0.085 to +0.296; H122 TP53 loss within KEAP1-loss cells for USP7 is +0.493, CI +0.351 to +0.635; H123 KEAP1 loss within ARID1A-loss cells for NFE2L2 is +0.776, CI +0.730 to +0.823; H126 SMARCA4 loss within high-ploidy cells for SMARCA2 is +0.772, CI +0.745 to +0.799. These are far above outcome-specific clinical thresholds and are accepted and closed as robustness strata. Formal lineage interactions were not decisive. H116 rejects the claimed adenocarcinoma-specific enhancement of the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2-dependency association: signed interaction -0.028, CI -0.076 to +0.020, with the positive upper bound below the approximate SMARCA2 threshold. H117 and H118 remain inconclusive for USP7 and STAT3 lineage heterogeneity: intervals are wide and include null, so I leave them unresolved and closed. H130 rejects the NF1-loss/stronger RIT1-dependency probe: signed estimate -0.021, CI -0.049 to +0.008, point in the opposite direction and upper bound below the approximate RIT1 threshold. Because H20 KEAP1 loss/weaker NFE2L2 dependency is now accepted across many strata but has not yet had independent validation, I request validation of H20. record.narrative:
This synthesis is the final scientific report for the current evidence in the supplied dataset.

New validation: H20 is independently validated and closed. KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. Discovery R8 signed estimate +0.796 (95% CI +0.776 to +0.816); independent validation R79 signed estimate +0.829 (independent CI +0.800 to +0.857). Both intervals exclude zero even at stricter validation alpha and are far above any ~10% relative difference threshold for NFE2L2 dependency. Because more negative scores mean stronger dependency, positive signed estimates mean KEAP1-loss cells have higher/less negative NFE2L2 scores, i.e. weaker dependency. This corroborates rejection of the original opposite-direction H8 claim.

Response deadline H96: the KRAS mutation effect in STK11-loss, TP53-wildtype cells had discovery R50 +0.052 (CI +0.008 to +0.096), but validation R53 +0.017 (independent CI -0.058 to +0.092). The validation point is below the approximate 10% relative threshold and does not reproduce the discovery effect, although the interval remains compatible with a clinically meaningful effect. I leave H96 unresolved and closed rather than reject, but this KRAS co-mutation refinement is not accepted and should not be promoted.

New validation H69: BRAF V600E versus RIT1 dependency is null/uncertain. Discovery R35 +0.004 (CI -0.025 to +0.033) and validation R80 -0.002 (independent CI -0.043 to +0.039). Both are imprecise, though validation includes clinically meaningful positive values; leave unresolved and closed with no further follow-up.

Current supported findings: independently validated dataset associations are H5 SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, H17 PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, H73 TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency, and H20 KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. H7 MSI-high with much stronger WRN dependency remains accepted on discovery and many robustness strata but is still the main core association not independently validated. All are observational associations among 2000 lung-cell-line profiles, not causal mechanisms or externally generalizable claims.

Negative or unsupported results remain informative: BRAF V600E did not support stronger BRAF dependency; ERBB2 amplification did not support overall ERBB2 dependency or adenocarcinoma-specific enhancement; ARID1A loss did not support SMARCA2 dependency; MYC amplification did not support POLR2A or USP7 dependencies; overall EGFR amplification failed to validate as a clinically meaningful effect; overall KRAS dependency was not decisive; lineage heterogeneity for SMARCA4/SMARCA2 was not supported; NF1 loss did not support RIT1 dependency; TP53 loss did not support stronger DHX9 dependency in the original direction.

Unresolved questions include conditional EGFR effects, KRAS co-mutation contexts after failed validation, formal lineage heterogeneity for USP7 and STAT3, research-marker/TMED10 signals, MYC-related RPL11 and KIF18A, TP53-MDM2 contexts, and BRCA2-related DHX9/WRN effects.

Most informative next analysis: request independent validation of H7 MSI-high and stronger WRN dependency. If it validates, close the core MSI/WRN claim; if it fails, reassess H7 as a discovery-only robust-stratum association. Otherwise, remaining analyses are lower priority explorations.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: The current evidence base is strongest for a small set of dataset-supported associations: SMARCA4 loss and much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, PTEN loss and stronger STAT3 dependency, TP53 loss and weaker USP7 dependency, KEAP1 loss and weaker NFE2L2 dependency, and MSI-high and much stronger WRN dependency. For the next analysis batch, I want to allocate discovery capacity in two ways: (1) test whether the accepted biology is recapitulated by alternative pathway alterations rather than merely the same marker, and (2) explore a few additional outcome-predictor pairs that are biologically plausible but have not yet been directly tested.  First, I register ERBB2 amplification, EGFR amplification, and PIK3CA mutation against STAT3 dependency. PTEN loss has already been validated as associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, so these claims test whether other RTK/PI3K-AKT pathway activations are associated with the same STAT3-dependency phenotype. These are clinically meaningful hypotheses: more negative STAT3 scores would mean stronger dependency, so I set the direction to -1 where a stronger association is the claimed direction.  Second, I register PIK3CA mutation against weaker USP7 dependency. Because TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency, PIK3CA activation could, if the effect is pathway-mediated, produce a comparable score shift in the positive direction, meaning less negative USP7 scores and weaker dependency. This is exploratory but directly tied to an accepted dataset association.  Third, I register MSI-high against DHX9 dependency. The MSI-high effect on WRN dependency is enormous and robust, but its specificity is not yet established. A strong MSI-high effect on DHX9 would broaden the DNA-repair dependency phenotype; a null or small result would support WRN specificity.  Fourth, I register NF1 loss against BRAF dependency. BRAF V600E itself did not support stronger BRAF dependency, and the previous NF1 loss probe for RIT1 was not supported, but MAPK-pathway co-dependencies remain a biologically useful hypothesis. I set this as uncertain rather than strongly anticipated.  Fifth, I register APC mutation against TMED10 dependency as a broad secretory/Wnt-associated probe, and CDKN2A loss against MDM2 dependency among TP53-wildtype cells as a p53-MDM2 regulatory-circuit probe. Both are new outcome-predictor pairs and should be judged against the approximate 10% relative threshold, about 0.025-0.03 mean-score shift for these outcomes.  Sixth, I add a direct squamous-cell refinement of the EGFR-amplification/KRAS-mutant conditional finding. The overall EGFR amplification claim remains unresolved after validation, but the KRAS-mutant stratum previously showed a potentially meaningful signed effect. Testing the squamous complement within KRAS-mutant cells helps determine whether that conditional signal is a lineage-specific artifact, a subgroup-specific signal, or not reproducible.  I am not registering further KRAS co-mutation claims at this stage because the KRAS/STK11/TP53 refinements failed or remained non-decisive after validation. In the next appraise stage, the highest-value validation action remains independent validation of H7, MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, if that has not already been delivered by the evaluator.

record.narrative: This batch uses all newly registered, still untested comparisons plus two direct lineage contrasts for accepted core outcomes. H133-H135 test whether alternative RTK/PI3K-AKT alterations (ERBB2 amplification, EGFR amplification, PIK3CA mutation) recapitulate the validated PTEN-loss association with stronger STAT3 dependency. H136 tests PIK3CA mutation against weaker USP7 dependency, and H141 tests PIK3CA mutation against EGFR dependency. H137 tests MSI-high against DHX9 dependency to probe specificity of the large MSI-high WRN phenotype. H138-H139 probe MAPK-pathway and secretory/Wnt-adjacent relationships (NF1 loss with BRAF dependency; APC mutation with TMED10 dependency). H140 tests CDKN2A loss within TP53-wildtype cells against MDM2 dependency, a p53-MDM2 circuit probe. H142 tests the EGFR-amplification effect specifically among KRAS-mutant squamous cells to clarify whether the prior KRAS-mutant conditional EGFR signal is lineage-specific. Finally, H131 and H132 test direct adenocarcinoma-versus-squamous contrasts for SMARCA2 and WRN dependency, because lineage subtype remains untested as a direct predictor for these accepted core outcomes and may be a useful confounding or effect-modifying context. I did not select already-validated or previously tested core claims in this discovery batch; the next independent validation priority remains H7 MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency.

record.narrative: All returned estimates are already signed to the hypothesis direction; positive values support the claimed association. I used approximate 10% clinical thresholds based on outcome scale: roughly 0.025 for BRAF/DHX9/EGFR/ERBB2/KIF18A/KRAS/TMED10, 0.027 for MDM2, 0.028 for STAT3, 0.018 for USP7, 0.030 for WRN, and 0.042 for SMARCA2. The strongest new result is H140: among TP53-wildtype cells, CDKN2A loss is associated with much stronger MDM2 dependency, signed estimate +0.119, 95% CI +0.079 to +0.158, exposed n=320. This is several times the approximate clinical threshold and excludes both null and small effects, so I accept it as a clinically meaningful dataset association. It remains observational and may be driven partly by correlated p16/p53-pathway biology or technical features, so I registered quality, proliferation, library, and p53-loss complement probes and would prioritize validation if budget allows. The requested validation this iteration remains H7 because closing the core MSI-high/WRN association was the preplanned highest-value validation target. The RTK/PI3K probes did not support a PTEN-like STAT3 phenotype. H133 ERBB2 amplification is imprecise and below threshold (H133 unresolved/closed); H135 PIK3CA mutation does not support clinically meaningful stronger STAT3 dependency and is rejected; H134 EGFR amplification points in the opposite direction, so I reject the original stronger-STAT3 claim while leaving open that it may be associated with weaker STAT3 dependency, which is not yet promoted. H136 PIK3CA mutation versus weaker USP7 dependency is suggestive but imprecise and left deferred. H137 MSI-high versus DHX9 dependency does not establish a broad MSI DNA-repair dependency phenotype and is left unresolved/closed; combined with the validated WRN result, it modestly supports WRN specificity but does not prove it. H138 NF1 loss versus BRAF dependency is rejected for the claimed direction; H139 APC mutation versus TMED10 is too small and imprecise to support the claim. H141 PIK3CA mutation versus EGFR dependency is rejected for the claimed direction. Direct lineage contrasts H131 and H132 are not decisive. H142 cannot be assessed because the squamous KRAS-mutant EGFR-amplified cell is too small. The multiplicity of this 12-test batch is not a concern for H140, whose effect is very large relative to noise, but it does argue against promoting any borderline probe.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: This synthesis closes H7 and H17 as independently validated dataset associations. H7, MSI-high versus WRN dependency signed for stronger dependency, has discovery R7 signed +0.790 with 95% CI +0.760 to +0.819 and validation R93 signed +0.805 with independent CI +0.758 to +0.851 at the stricter validation alpha. The effect is far above the approximate 10% clinical threshold for WRN and excludes both null and clinically small effects under the validation interval. H17, PTEN loss versus stronger STAT3 dependency, has discovery R24 signed +0.267 with 95% CI +0.215 to +0.319 and validation R66 signed +0.307 with independent CI +0.228 to +0.387, also far above the approximate 10% threshold for STAT3. These are observational associations in the supplied lung-cell-line profiles, not causal mechanisms or externally generalizable claims. H2 is assessed as rejected for the original claim that EGFR amplification is associated with clinically meaningful stronger EGFR dependency: discovery R2 is borderline and imprecise, with a signed estimate near the threshold but an interval that includes the null, and validation R13 has a below-threshold signed estimate with an interval compatible with no meaningful effect. Current supported findings are SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, MSI-high with much stronger WRN dependency, and CDKN2A loss in TP53-wildtype cells with stronger MDM2 dependency, with the first five now independently validated and the sixth accepted on strong discovery evidence but not yet independently validated. Negative findings include lack of clinically meaningful support for overall EGFR amplification, ERBB2 amplification, PIK3CA mutation, NF1-loss BRAF or RIT1 associations, APC mutation with TMED10, MYC amplification with POLR2A or USP7, ARID1A loss with SMARCA2, and BRAF V600E with BRAF dependency. KRAS overall and several conditional EGFR or KRAS contexts remain unresolved or failed validation. Unresolved questions include conditional EGFR in KRAS-mutant cells, research-marker TMED10 probes, MYC-high POLR2A or RPL11 effects, STK11 and TP53 co-mutation contexts, lineage heterogeneity for accepted associations, BRCA2-related DHX9 or WRN effects, and TP53-loss MDM2 complements. The most informative next analysis is independent validation of H140 in the next appraise because it is the strongest new accepted effect, CDKN2A loss in TP53-wildtype cells associated with much stronger MDM2 dependency, signed +0.119 with 95% CI +0.079 to +0.158, several times the approximate clinical threshold and large enough that multiplicity concerns are modest. After that, analyze the already registered robustness strata H143 to H146 and the TP53-loss complement H147. If validation budget remains, secondary candidates are H90, conditional EGFR in KRAS-mutant cells, or H4, overall KRAS mutation versus KRAS dependency, but H140 is the highest-value priority.
