Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative:
The highest-priority current evidence question is to establish whether the newly accepted H140 finding is robust and reasonably specific rather than an incidental co-deletion or batch signal. I therefore register mechanistic follow-ups for MDM2 dependency: MTAP loss in TP53-wildtype cells, and CDKN2A loss among MTAP-intact TP53-wildtype cells. The first asks whether a common 9p21/MTAP deletion context tracks MDM2 dependency; the second asks whether the accepted CDKN2A association can persist when MTAP loss is absent, which would strengthen specificity to CDKN2A rather than broad locus co-deletion. I also register a screen_batch stratification because H140 is large but still discovery-only. These should be interpreted against an approximate MDM2 clinical threshold near 0.027 mean-score units; H140's +0.119 is far above that, so the new probes are mainly for specificity and technical robustness rather than for detecting marginal effects.

I also register two specificity probes for accepted pathway associations. For USP7, TP53 loss is validated as associated with weaker USP7 dependency, implying that p53-pathway intact cells are relatively more USP7-dependent. Testing PTEN loss within TP53-wildtype cells asks whether another tumor-suppressor loss produces a comparable USP7 phenotype. This is not strongly anticipated, but a clear null would support specificity to TP53 status. For STAT3, PTEN loss is validated as associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. Testing TP53 loss within PTEN-wildtype cells asks whether p53-pathway loss is independently associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, a plausible inflammation or stress-signaling effect but one that should not be assumed because PTEN and TP53 can co-occur.

Finally, I register a conditional EGFR-amplification test among KRAS-mutant adenocarcinoma cells. H90 suggested a potentially meaningful positive signed effect in all KRAS-mutant cells, with a signed estimate of +0.053 and a 95% interval +0.004 to +0.103, above the approximate 0.025 EGFR threshold. Squamous KRAS-mutant EGFR-amplified cells were too sparse, so a direct adenocarcinoma stratum may give a more stable view of whether this conditional signal is localized to the dominant histologic subgroup. All proposed comparisons are still observational hypotheses; none should be interpreted as causal mechanisms or external generalization until evidence and independent validation are assessed.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. record.narrative: All estimates are already signed to the claim direction, so positive values support stronger MDM2 dependency for the CDKN2A-loss claims. H143 through H146 are highly reassuring robustness strata of H140: CDKN2A loss among TP53-wildtype cells showed signed effects of +0.113, +0.117, +0.130, and +0.134 under higher Cas9 activity, Avana library, faster proliferation, and higher screen ROC, respectively. Each 95% lower bound was above the MDM2 clinical threshold, so I accept these as clinically meaningful within-stratum dataset associations and close them as robustness probes. H149 is important for specificity: CDKN2A loss retained a signed effect of +0.106 with lower bound +0.063 among TP53-wildtype cells without MTAP loss, supporting that the H140 signal is not solely a broad 9p21 MTAP co-deletion proxy. H147 shows a similar effect in TP53-loss cells, signed +0.111 with lower bound +0.035. I accept this as evidence that CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency in this p53-loss complement as well, but it weakens any interpretation that the H140 association is strictly TP53-wildtype-specific. It should still be read as observational and possibly related to co-deleted loci or p53-pathway context, not as a causal mechanism. H150 in batch_a has a large point estimate, +0.098, and excludes the null, but its lower bound +0.023 is just below the approximate 0.027 threshold, so I do not consider it decisive for clinical meaningfulness; it is left unresolved and closed, while arguing against a gross batch_a-only artifact. H148, MTAP loss alone in TP53-wildtype cells, has a below-threshold point estimate and an interval that includes both null and clinically meaningful positive values, so it remains unresolved and closed as not informative enough to promote MTAP. For specificity probes, H151 rejects PTEN loss as associated with weaker USP7 dependency within TP53-wildtype cells: the signed estimate is opposite the claim and the upper interval is below the USP7 threshold. H152 rejects TP53 loss as associated with stronger STAT3 dependency within PTEN-wildtype cells: the estimate is essentially null and the upper interval is below the STAT3 threshold. H153 and H31 are unresolved: EGFR amplification among KRAS-mutant adenocarcinoma cells is imprecise and below the EGFR threshold, and KRAS mutation among adenocarcinoma cells is small and imprecise with an interval spanning null and meaningful positive effects. Neither establishes a clinically meaningful association, so I defer the EGFR-KRAS-adenocarcinoma probe and close the adenocarcinoma KRAS probe. record.narrative: This exploration prioritizes formal context modification around independently validated dependencies rather than adding weak marginal probes. In the supplied lung-cell-line dataset, a relative 10 percent scale corresponds roughly to 0.02 to 0.03 dependency-score units on these scales, and several accepted effects are far above that. For MDM2, H140 was independently validated, and accepted strata H147 and H149 suggest the CDKN2A association is not narrowly limited to TP53-wildtype or MTAP-intact cells. The registered CDKN2A by MTAP interaction among TP53-wildtype cells asks whether the signed CDKN2A effect is larger when MTAP is co-lost, attenuated, or unchanged; alternatives are a broad 9p21 deletion effect, a CDKN2A-specific effect, or no meaningful effect modification. For SMARCA2, H5 is validated; the SMARCA4 by ARID1A interaction tests whether co-loss of another SWI/SNF subunit modifies the synthetic-lethal-like association. For NFE2L2 and STAT3, H20 and H17 are validated; TP53 interactions test whether p53-pathway loss formally modifies the KEAP1 or PTEN effects rather than merely co-occurring with them. For USP7, H73 is validated; the TP53 by MYC-amplification interaction asks whether the TP53 effect differs between MYC-amplified and MYC-intact cells. For WRN, H7 is validated; MSI-high dependency among BRCA2-intact cells tests whether the MSI effect survives after excluding BRCA2-loss cells, although the overlap between MSI-high and BRCA2-loss cells should be monitored. For POLR2A and RPL11, MYC amplification alone was not accepted, so MYC-expression interactions test whether expression-competent MYC amplification creates clinically meaningful dependency only when accompanied by high MYC expression. All proposed comparisons remain observational hypotheses in this dataset; effect modification, specificity, and robustness are not causal claims or external generalizability.

record.narrative: No discovery assessments are due. I request 12 currently untested analyses that test context dependence, technical robustness, and specificity of the strongest accepted associations while avoiding known sparse cells. H154 and H155 ask whether the MDM2-CDKN2A association is formally modified by TP53 status or by MTAP co-loss within TP53-wildtype cells, distinguishing a broad 9p21 co-deletion pattern from a context-specific CDKN2A association. H156 tests whether ARID1A co-loss modifies SMARCA2 dependency in the SMARCA4-loss context. H157 and H158 test whether TP53 loss formally modifies the KEAP1/NFE2L2 and PTEN/STAT3 associations rather than merely co-occurring with them. H159 tests whether MYC amplification modifies the USP7-TP53 association, while H100 through H102 test whether library choice or Cas9 activity formally modifies USP7 and STAT3 associations, complementing the accepted robustness and non-Avana validation results. H160 checks whether the WRN MSI-high association remains after excluding BRCA2-loss cells, assessing possible co-driver confounding. H161 and H162 test MYC-expression-dependent MYC-amplification effects for POLR2A and RPL11, addressing whether MYC-amplified associations require expression-competent MYC rather than genomic amplification alone. These analyses are exploratory and in the supplied dataset only; significant interactions or robustness strata would indicate context-specific associations, not causal mechanism or external generalizability.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All estimates are signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive values support the registered direction and negative values oppose it. I used approximate 10 percent outcome-scale thresholds: about 0.027 for MDM2, 0.042 for SMARCA2, 0.009 for NFE2L2, 0.028 for STAT3, 0.018 for USP7, 0.030 for WRN, 0.026 for POLR2A, and 0.025 for RPL11. For MDM2, H154 was very small in the opposite direction and the interval was symmetric around null, so it provides no clinically meaningful TP53 effect modification; H155 supported a CDKN2A-by-MTAP interaction with a point above threshold but the wide interval included null and both clinically meaningful directions, so it is not decisive. Both are left unresolved and closed as low-information specificity probes. H156 tests whether ARID1A co-loss modifies the very large SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association; its signed effect is below the SMARCA2 threshold and imprecise, so there is not enough evidence for a meaningful modification. H157 for NFE2L2/KEAP1 by TP53 loss is small relative to the main KEAP1 effect and imprecise, so it is also unresolved. For STAT3, H158 rejects the registered direction: the signed interval upper bound is below the clinical threshold and the point estimate is opposite the hypothesis. The raw sign suggests attenuation of the PTEN-STAT3 association in TP53-loss cells, but that is a data-driven reversal after multiple interaction tests; I did not accept it, and I registered a separate reversed interaction proposal as a follow-up candidate only. For USP7, H159 has a large point estimate but an interval that includes null and spans both directions, so it is closed as underpowered; H100 and H101 are formal technical-context interactions but are extremely imprecise because the complement cells are small, so they remain unresolved and closed. H160 is a strong positive specificity result: among BRCA2-intact cells, MSI-high remains associated with much stronger WRN dependency, with a lower bound far above threshold. This supports the robustness and co-driver specificity of the validated MSI-high WRN association. For MYC-expression interactions, H161 rejects the registered POLR2A hypothesis because the signed estimate is opposite and the upper bound is below threshold; H162 for RPL11 has a point just below threshold and a wide interval spanning null, so it is unresolved. The only new result warranting independent validation is H102, the STAT3 PTEN-by-library interaction: it has a lower bound above threshold, but it rests on a small non-Avana complement and conflicts with the already validated non-Avana PTEN effect from H58. I therefore leave H102 active and request validation before accepting any library-context effect modification. These remain observational findings in the supplied dataset; none establishes causality or external generalizability.
